target_customer: Shipping lines operating container ships (CMA CGM ran pilots)
problem: Ships are mostly operated by crew with limited perception aids; Shone retrofits existing cargo ships with autonomy software and sensors to help crews and move toward autonomous operation.
business_model: Retrofit hardware and software deals with shipping lines

founders.name: Ugo Vollmer
founders.background_notes: Named by TechCrunch June 2018; no background in that article.

founders.name: Antoine de Maleprade
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as Founder/CTO with no background.

technical_complexity.rationale: Perception and autonomy for ships operating at sea, retrofit onto varied vessels, with maritime regulatory limits.

defensibility.rationale: Pilots with a major carrier and integration into ships create stickiness, but large marine suppliers had more resources.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Per one report Kongsberg bought Rolls-Royce's autonomous marine unit in 2018; Shone itself is reported acquired in 2022 by a single database.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in June 2018 described interest in automating container ships; CMA CGM later piloted Shone software on several ships.

brand_strength.rationale: Covered by TechCrunch and trade press for its CMA CGM pilot, but no distinct brand asset or community was found.

outcome_analysis: Shone raised a 4 million dollar seed in June 2018 and piloted retrofit autonomy software with CMA CGM, and one database reports it was acquired by Bedrock Ocean Exploration in April 2022. The YC directory lists it as inactive; no shutdown or post-mortem was found, so this reads as an exit or soft landing whose terms are not public.
notes: shone.com did not resolve from this session, so the site could not be read. The seed is stated by TechCrunch and Alven (Alven page carries conflicting dates, with 28 June 2018 most likely original). The 2022 acquisition rests on a single database (CB Insights) and is unverified. A search summary says the founders were Parisian classmates Ugo Vollmer, Clement Renault and de Maleprade, but no opened source confirmed Renault, so he is not listed. Competitor search found Kongsberg, Rolls-Royce and Yara Birkeland as incumbents but no page I could date at or before the batch, so competitors are empty.
